sentences.text:
Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr on 31
July, 2017
Author: V.K. Bist

Bench: V.K. Bist
In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Criminal Writ Petition No.1046 of 2012
Sudhir Kapoor & another ......Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another ...Respondents
Mr. Jagdish Chandra Belwal and Mr. Suresh Kumar Mishra, Advocates for the petitioners.
Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, Aga for the State of Uttarakhand.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Dated: 31.07.2017 Hon'ble V.K. Bist J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Present petition has been filed for the following relief:
"i. Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order (annexure-4) dated 24.09.2012 passed by respondent no.2 in case no.51/5 of 2012 State of Uttarakhand vs. Chandra Kishore and others."

entities.text: case no.51/5 of 2012 State of Uttarakhand vs. Chandra Kishore and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the Act)
provides for establishment of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal to hear appeals from the decisions of the Adjudicating Officer under section 68 of the Act.
At the time when order dated 24.09.2012 was passed, Food Safety Appellate Tribunal was not functioning.
Therefore, the petitioner had no efficacious alternative remedy except to approach this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
The writ petition filed by the petitioner was entertained and on 01.11.2012 following order was passed:-

"Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners and taking note of the endorsement made by the Registry, it is pertinent to mention that Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) is meant for preferring appeal before the High Court against the decision or order of a Special Court.

Those Special Courts are constituted u/s 74 of the Act for the purposes of trial of offences Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr on 31 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87439967/
1 relating to grievous injury or death of the consumer for which punishment of imprisonment for more than three years has been prescribed under the Act.

entities.text: Sudhir Kapoor And Anr vs State Of Uttarakhand And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said Section further provides that these special courts shall be constituted by the Central or the State Government, as the case may be, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.

Learned counsel has argued that the present petition has been filed assailing the adjudication done by the Additional District Magistrate of District U.S. Nagar u/s 68 of the Act and against such adjudication, the appeal shall be preferred before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal established u/s 70 of the Act.

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate of District U.S. Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A further enactment has been made that against the judgment of Tribunal, an appeal can be preferred before the High Court, as envisaged u/s 71(6) of the Act.

Learned counsel has argued that since no such Tribunal has been established in the State of Uttarakhand within the meaning of Section 70 of the Act, thus, the petitioners have no option but to approach this Court by way of instant petition u/s 226/227 of the Constitution of India, against the order of Adjudicating Officer, who is of the rank of Additional District Magistrate.
The Court is quite convinced with this argument and thus, admits the petition for hearing.

Registry is directed to summon the record of case no.51/5 of 2012, titled as 'State of Uttarakhand Vs. Chand Kishore and others', from the court of Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, U.S. Nagar.

entities.text: State of Uttarakhand Vs. Chand Kishore and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, U.S. Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List after six weeks.

Meanwhile, the fine, so imposed against the petitioners, by way of impugned judgment, shall remain stayed provided the petitioners deposit half of the fine as per rules before the Adjudicating Officer, U.S. Nagar, within two weeks from today.

Stay application no.11839 of 2012 is disposed of accordingly."
4.
Today learned counsel for the parties submit that Food Safety Tribunal has already been established at Haldwani.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that he may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition enabling him to approach Food Safety Tribunal.
6. Permission is granted.
7. The writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioner to approach the Food Safety Tribunal.
